newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor to retire power barges.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor to retire power barges.

text.p: The Philippines' National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Monday it will retire four power barges with capacity totalling 500 megawatts starting next year.
Napocor chairman Francisco Viray told reporters the five-year contracts covering the bunker-fired power plants would not be renewed as power plants running on cheaper fuel came on stream.

Viray said the 600-mw Masinloc coal-fired power project in Zambales, north of the capital, was commissioned this year while the 720-mw Pagbilao coal-based plant in Quezon, south of Manila, would be operational next year.
"We will be increasing the availability of the less costly power plants and this will mean lower rates," Viray said.
Napocor resorted to using power barges leased from private power firms in 1993 during the height of the country's severe power shortfalls.
The independent power producers that rented out the facilities were Sabah Shipyard of Malaysia, East Asia Power Corp and Far East Levingston Shipbuildings of Singapore.
